results.content: Moreover, none of these toolkits integrate heterophilic hypergraph datasets, which represent a particularly challenging setting (Li et al., 2025c), nor do they support graph-level tasks (e.g., hypergraph classification). These limitations significantly restrict the reproducibility and comprehensive evaluation of advanced HNNs. To bridge the gap, we propose DHG-Bench, which serves as the first open-sourced and comprehensive benchmark for HNNs. Our benchmark encompasses 17 representative HNN methods and 22 diverse hypergraph datasets covering node-level, edge-level, and graph-level tasks. To answer this question, we evaluate the performance of HNN methods on diverse, widely used hypergraph datasets across three benchmark tasks: node classification, hyperedge prediction, and hypergraph classification. • Walmart (Chien et al., 2022): The Walmart dataset models a hypergraph where nodes represent products and hyperedges capture sets of products purchased together. For evaluation, we follow prior studies in choosing task-specific metrics: accuracy for node classification (Feng et al., 2019; Chien et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2023a); AUROC (area under the ROC curve) and AP (average precision) for hyperedge prediction (Hwang et al., 2022; Ko et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2025; Tang et al., 2025); and both accuracy and Macro-F1 score for hypergraph classification (Feng et al., 2024). To analyze structure-level robustness, follow-ing (Cai et al., 2022), we randomly remove or add a proportion of node–hyperedge connections (i.e., hyperlinks) in the original hypergraph and then train and evaluate HNN algorithms on the perturbed structures. results.title: Hypergraph contrastive attention networks for hyperedge prediction with negative samples evaluation - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Hypergraph contrastive attention networks for hyperedge prediction with negative samples evaluation. However, these approaches involve two issues: (i) in hyperedge feature learning, they fail to measure the influence of nodes on the hyperedges that include them and the neighboring hyperedges, and (ii) in the binary classification task, the quality of the generated negative samples directly impacts the prediction results. To this end, we propose a Hypergraph Contrastive Attention Network (HCAN) model for hyperedge prediction. Accordingly, a variety of tasks related to hypergraphs have emerged, e.g., link prediction (Chai, Tu, Wang, & Su, 2024), node classification (Wu et al., 2024), hyperedge prediction (Hwang et al., 2022, Kumar et al., 2020). The emergence of deep learning provides a straightforward solution for hyperedge prediction: employing HyperGraph Neural Networks (HGNNs) for feature learning and conducting binary prediction on a given set of hyperedges (Bai et al., 2021, Ju et al., 2024, Yadati et al., 2019, Zhang et al., 2020). Hypergraph-based neural networks for hyperedge prediction are usually categorized into two types during feature learning. By capturing the spatio-temporal relations among higher-order structures within dynamic hypergraphs, many models can effectively perform prediction tasks with time (Tian et al., 2023, Wang, Zhang, et al., 2024). After modeling hyperedge prediction as a classification task, the quality of generated negative samples can directly affect the prediction performance of models (Hwang et al., 2022, Patil et al., 2020, Yadati et al., 2020). Further, the methodology part is organized as follows: Section 4.1 describes the hypergraph relation matrix obtained by processing the input hypergraph; Section 4.2 constructs the hypergraph contrastive attention network, which includes two attention encoders and one simple encoder without attention; Section 4.3 performs contrastive attention learning. We present the hypergraph contrastive attention network, which aims to address the key challenge of hyperedge prediction. Our model enhances the performance of hyperedge predictions across varying orders through the order propagation attention mechanism, which refines attention computation and improves information aggregation. Recent studies have extended graph convolutional networks and contrastive learning to hypergraphs, but it encounters two issues posed by hyperedge heterogeneity: (i) message-passing based hypergraph neural networks let node mix different neighbor information within heterogeneous hyperedges, resulting in poor representation learning. * ### Hypergraph Semi-Supervised Contrastive Learning for Hyperedge Prediction Based on Enhanced Attention Aggregator.
